description:
FOUND s437 (Fable review) while attributing the companion mover op/utf8cache.t
DIFF 2/0 -> TIMEOUT 2/0.  C_ok is unchanged; the STATUS moved because the
#467 recovery load (s434) now carries the file past its first dying form into
the test that reads

    { local ${^UTF8CACHE} = 1;
      my $x = "\x{100}" x 1000000;
      while ($x =~ /./g) { my $p = pos($x); }
      pass("quadratic pos"); }

whose whole point is "this must not go quadratic".  Under PCL it does.

MEASURED (runpcl, ~1.45 s of that is SBCL startup):
    100k chars, /./g + pos()          5.60 s
    200k chars, /./g + pos()         17.11 s      (2x data -> ~3.8x time: QUADRATIC)
    100k chars, /./g, NO pos()        5.60 s      (pos() is NOT the cost)
    100k ASCII "a", /./g + pos()      5.60 s      (wide chars are NOT the cost)
    100k ASCII "a", /./g, no pos()    5.30 s
    perl, 1M chars                    0.09 s
So every scalar-context /g match does O(length) work before/after the scan
itself -- 40 us per match at 100k, 80 us at 200k.  Projected 1M: ~400 s, which
is why the file TIMEOUTs at 90 s (and under the snapshot's `--load` runner the
file died BEFORE reaching this loop, hence DIFF 2/0 there).

THE CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (not taken here): sb-sprof on the qp6
shape (`my $x = "a" x 100000; while ($x =~ /./g) { $n++ }`) in the p-match
path.  Suspects, in order: (1) the subject string is COPIED or COERCED per call
(subseq from pos / coerce to simple-string / a displaced-array fix-up) instead
of handing cl-ppcre the same string with :start pos; (2) the scanner is rebuilt
per call (the literal regex should hit the compiled-scanner cache -- check the
cache key); (3) pos bookkeeping that walks the string (a char<->byte offset
conversion, or magic lookup that scans).  Whichever it is, the fix is runtime
(cl/pcl-runtime.lisp), so the full sweep is its gate (WHAT-TO-RUN table) plus
the op/ companion leg; acceptance = the 1M-char loop under 5 s and
op/utf8cache.t back to DIFF (C_ok > 2) without a timeouts.tsv allowance.

Target A (speed must beat perl): this is a 1000x gap on a common idiom
(tokenisers, parsers, `while (/\G.../gc)` loops), so it is worth a filler
soon even though no row count sits behind it today.


SHIPPED s450u (Opus, round 8 agent U, 2026-08-29).

THE MECHANISM, found by the sb-sprof run this task asked for (100k `while
($x =~ /./g) { }`, 3 672 samples):

    pcl::set-match-vars        94.2 % total
    sb-kernel:vector-subseq    73.7 % total
    gc_alloc_large             43.3 % total

`set-match-vars` built all three match variables eagerly on every successful
match, and two of them are the whole subject: `$\`` is `(subseq str 0 start)`
and `$'` is `(subseq str end)`.  N matches therefore copied the subject 2N
times — the quadratic term.  Neither of this task's other suspects was the
cost: the scanner IS cached and the subject is NOT copied by `to-string`.

THE FIX (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp only): a successful match records the subject
and two fixnums (`*match-subject*` / `*match-beg*` / `*match-end*`), and
`|$&|`, `` |$`| `` and `|$'| ` become `define-symbol-macro`s over accessors
that cut — and memoise — on the first READ.  perl's own rule.  Writers exist
(`(setf %match-whole)` etc.) because the s///e path sets `$&` directly and
because generated code must still COMPILE if a program names one as an
assignment target.  `clear-capture-groups` forgets the match instead of
assigning nil.

    while ($x =~ /./g) { }      runpcl wall (~0.20 s is startup)
         n        before     after
         1 000     0.18 s     0.23 s
        50 000     1.08 s     0.37 s
       100 000     3.37 s     0.48 s
       200 000    12.80 s     0.72 s      <- 17.8x
       400 000       --       1.26 s
     1 000 000       --       2.83 s      (was projected ~400 s; perl 0.09 s)

Doubling the data now doubles the time.  ACCEPTANCE MET: the 1M loop is under
5 s and `t/op/utf8cache.t` goes TIMEOUT 2/0 -> **DIFF 14/0** (perl side 16/0),
verified by `tools/run-perl-suite.pl op/utf8cache.t`, parallel and serial
agreeing.  Its one dropped statement is the census's existing row.  The
snapshot row was NOT edited (Fable splices at merge).

WHY SYMBOL MACROS AND NOT THE EXISTING `p-magic-cell` BOX (`$.`'s mechanism,
rule 11's first question): a magic-cell box is a SHARED CONTAINER, so every
site that stores the variable stores the same box and every reader then sees
the CURRENT match.  Probed on `$.`, which has that representation: `push
@lines, $.` prints `3 3 3` where perl prints `1 2 3` — a live silent wrong,
filed as #683.  A symbol macro keeps the value an ordinary string at every use
site.  Its price is that `boundp`/`symbol-value` stop answering, so the ONE
place that reads a magic scalar through its symbol —
`%p-symref-scalar-value`, the `${"&"}` spelling from #505 — consults a
three-entry getter table.  Measured in SBCL first: a `let` of a symbol-macro
name is legal (it shadows), so the `local $&` emission still compiles.

WHAT A DEFERRED CUT RELIES ON, and it is not free: the subject must not be
mutated in place between the match and the read, or `$x =~ /cd/;
substr($x,0,1) = "Z"` would answer from the new contents.  Every string writer
in this runtime builds a new string (`copy-seq`/`concatenate`: `p-vec-set`,
the magic string increment, lvalue and 4-arg `substr`, `tr///`, `chop`), all
probed against perl.  Stated normatively in `docs/ir-spec.md` §8 and guarded
in `Pl/t/match-vars-01.t` (28 -> 31 rows: the mutation family, the `${"&"}`
spelling, and a memoised read followed by a new match).

13 probes vs perl 5.40.3, byte-identical: basic partition, a failed match
keeping the old values, /g with pos, pos written, the four mutation
spellings, s/// and s///e, a utf8 subject, `${"&"}`/`${"\`"}`/`${"'"}`, read
twice then re-match.

NO generation bump (cl/-only).  RESIDUE FILED: #680 — still ~2.6 us per match
against perl's 0.09 us, with the profile recipe and three suspects (the
@-/@+ rebuild, `clear-capture-groups`' 20 unconditional writes, the scanner
cache key).
subject: Target-A: a scalar-context `m//g` loop is QUADRATIC -- `while ($x =~ /./g) {}` over 100k chars takes 4 s, 200k 15.7 s (perl: 1M chars in 0.09 s); t/op/utf8cache.t "quadratic pos" TIMEOUTs on it
